universal.label: UK Emergency Services (Police, Ambulance, Fire, Coastguard)
universal.description: Primary UK emergency number for life-threatening situations. 112 also works identically across all UK mobile and fixed networks.

categories.name: Police & Public Safety
categories.description: Emergency 999 police response and 101 non-emergency crime reporting.

numbers.label: Emergency Police Dispatch
numbers.audience: Anyone facing immediate danger, violence, or a crime currently in progress.
numbers.whenToUse: Call immediately if an offender is still at the scene or someone is in physical danger. If you cannot speak, press 55 when prompted (Silent Solution).

numbers.label: Police Non-Emergency Number
numbers.audience: Residents reporting past crimes (stolen car, property damage) where the offender has left and no one is in immediate danger.
numbers.whenToUse: Use 101 to report non-urgent crimes or give information to local police without tying up 999 emergency operators.

categories.name: Medical & NHS
categories.description: 999 critical ambulance dispatch, NHS 111 urgent medical advice, and mental health support.

numbers.label: NHS Emergency Ambulance
numbers.audience: Patients with life-threatening emergencies such as cardiac arrest, stroke, severe breathing difficulty, or major trauma.
numbers.whenToUse: Call 999 immediately when someone is seriously ill or injured and their life is at risk.

numbers.label: NHS 111 Urgent Medical & Mental Health Triage
numbers.audience: Anyone with an urgent medical or mental health problem who is unsure whether to go to A&E.
numbers.whenToUse: Call 111 when you need urgent medical help fast, or select the mental health option for immediate NHS crisis team support.

numbers.label: Samaritans Crisis & Emotional Support
numbers.audience: Anyone in emotional distress, struggling to cope, or at risk of suicide.
numbers.whenToUse: Call anytime day or night for free, confidential listening and crisis support.

categories.name: Fire, Rescue & Coastguard
categories.description: Fire & Rescue Services and HM Coastguard maritime/coastal rescue.

numbers.label: Fire & Rescue / HM Coastguard
numbers.audience: Anyone reporting a fire, trapped person, chemical spill, or coastal/sea emergency.
numbers.whenToUse: Dial 999 (or 112) and ask the operator for 'Fire' or 'Coastguard'.

categories.name: Women & Child Safety
categories.description: National Domestic Abuse Helpline and Childline support.

numbers.label: National Domestic Abuse Helpline (Refuge)
numbers.audience: Women and individuals experiencing domestic violence, coercive control, or abuse.
numbers.whenToUse: Call for confidential refuge placement, safety planning, and crisis support (call 999 if in immediate physical danger).

numbers.label: Childline UK
numbers.audience: Children and young people under 19 facing abuse, bullying, neglect, or danger.
numbers.whenToUse: Call anytime for confidential support; the call will not appear on the phone bill.

categories.name: Highway & Cyber Crime
categories.description: National Highways motorway breakdown line and Action Fraud cyber reporting.

numbers.label: National Highways Motorway Helpline
numbers.audience: Drivers stranded on motorways or major A-roads in England (not in a live lane).
numbers.whenToUse: If stopped in a live motorway lane, call 999 immediately. Use 0300 123 5000 for hard-shoulder assistance or hazard reporting.

numbers.label: Action Fraud (UK National Fraud & Cyber Crime Centre)
numbers.audience: Individuals and small businesses targeted by online scams, banking fraud, or hacking.
numbers.whenToUse: Call to report cyber crime and financial fraud directly to the National Fraud Intelligence Bureau.
numbers.coverage: England, Wales & Northern Ireland (call 101 in Scotland)
